verdict.rationale: Lium is a GPU rental marketplace, so a spot or interruptible tier is a fair question to ask of it. The evidence, however, documents only on-demand per-second billing, cheapest-node rental under a `max_price_per_gpu_hour` ceiling, and e-mail notice before price raises. Nothing describes a discounted interruptible tier or the preemption semantics (eviction notice, reclaim behavior). The price ceiling and per-second billing are adjacent cost controls, not spot capacity, so they earn no credit.

support.subject: As an ML engineer, I can rent spot or interruptible GPU capacity at a deep discount with clearly documented preemption semantics
